case_title: Jagga Singh and Anr. v. State of Punjab
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; IPC s.307; IPC s.325 r/w s.34
evidence_type: Medical (post-mortem report); prosecution account of the incident and gunshot sounds; admitted gunshot injury
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.307 IPC; 7 years RI and fine for Jagga Singh; Jagtar Singh and Kaka Singh also sentenced to 7 years RI and fine
high_court_outcome: Accused appeals dismissed; State appeal allowed and accused convicted under s.302
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that at about 8.30 p.m. on 24 April 1992, three accused persons came to a house in a village. One of the accused fired a gun at the first victim, striking his right thigh, and the first victim fell down. The accused then took the second victim away towards a nearby village. About twenty minutes later, the sound of three or four gunshots was heard from that direction. The dead body of the second victim was found the next morning. The post-mortem examination of the second victim's body recorded only lacerated wounds, and no gunshot wound was found on it. The gunshot injury to the first victim's leg was admitted. The evidence therefore consisted of the account of the events at the house, the admitted firearm injury, the timing of the gunfire sounds, the discovery of the body and the post-mortem findings. The prosecution relied on these facts to establish the incident and the injuries caused during it.
physical_harm: First victim suffered a gunshot injury to the leg (leg/thigh wound, grievous hurt under s.325 finding); second victim found dead the next morning, with only lacerated wounds and no gunshot wound on post-mortem
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.302 and s.307, each with s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.325 r/w s.34)
key_evidence_accepted: Admitted gunshot injury to the first victim's leg; post-mortem report showing no gunshot wound on the second victim's body
bail_history: Sentence suspended pending appeal by order of 14.09.2007 on personal bonds of Rs. 20,000 each with two sureties of Rs. 10,000 each
trial_duration: offence: 24.4.92; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 04.12.2006; Supreme Court: 03.02.2011
legal_representation: Accused (appellants): Rajiv Garg, Ashish Garg and Annam D.N. Rao. State: Kuldip Singh
investigation_status: Not stated (post-mortem examination conducted; body found next morning)
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.307 with 7 years RI and fine. High Court: accused's appeals dismissed; State's appeal allowed and convicted under s.302. Supreme Court: acquitted of s.302; convicted under s.325 r/w s.34; sentence of period undergone
legal_principle_applied: Benefit of doubt where the post-mortem findings created doubt about the prosecution version of a gunshot death; joint liability under s.34 for the admitted gunshot injury
sentencing_rationale: Sentence limited to the period already undergone for the s.325 r/w s.34 conviction; no reasons stated beyond this
